candidate_results.name: Nested Invariant Stack
candidate_results.design_sol_read: The centralized kernel remains mechanically robust, but at MICRO/COMPACT scale it carries too much identity weight as one bounded emblem-like object. It therefore does not earn survivor status in this construction even though the same kernel persists across roles.
candidate_results.refinement_boundary: Any later CPS-A refinement must be a separately authorized refinement path; do not tune this consumed comparison carrier after result exposure.

candidate_results.name: Distributed Recognition Mesh
candidate_results.design_sol_read: Strongest architecture. Identity remains recoverable through redundant structural carriers under crop, scale, no-image, forced-color and APP/WEB changes without requiring one central emblem or contextual scene.
candidate_results.usage_restraint: Keep the mesh sparse and truthful; redundancy must not become a decorative inventory of identity marks.

candidate_results.name: Context-Persistent Presence Scaffold
candidate_results.design_sol_read: The persistent scaffold survives alone and translates cleanly while leaving more room for relational composition than CPS-A. It clears the promotion floor, but its thesis creates a material risk that context could become identity authority if usage discipline weakens.
candidate_results.usage_restraint: Context may expand, position or relate the Character but must never substitute for, mirror-mutate, or carry required canonical identification.

comparative_conclusion.recommendation_reason: CPS-B provides the strongest redundant identity recovery across scale/crop/accessibility and optional depiction loss while avoiding CPS-A central-emblem pressure and relying less on relational/contextual support than CPS-C.
comparative_conclusion.director_question: Which surviving canonical Character-presence architecture should become the Phase C incumbent: CPS-B Distributed Recognition Mesh, or CPS-C Context-Persistent Presence Scaffold under its context-dependency restraint?
